core_loop.name: Play a level
core_loop.description: Short, goal-driven match-3 levels with a move limit; power-up creation and combos are the skill expression.

steps.action: start the next level from the castle screen
swap adjacent tiles to match 3+ and build power-ups toward the level goals
meet every goal within the move limit
accept extra moves for coins, or fail and lose a life

meta_loops.name: Restore the castle
meta_loops.description: Stars from wins are spent on visible renovation tasks; finishing an area opens the next one.

steps.action: spend stars on the next renovation task
complete all tasks in an area
steps.reward: area completion reward and a new area

meta_loops.name: Team support
meta_loops.description: Teams let players ask for and send lives, turning waiting into a social exchange.

steps.action: request lives from teammates when out of lives
send lives to teammates who ask

mechanics.name: Swap to match
rules: Swapping two adjacent tiles is legal only if it creates a match of 3 or more
Matched tiles clear, tiles above fall, new tiles refill from the top
dynamics: Players scan the lower board first because clears there cause more cascades

mechanics.name: Shape-based power-ups
rules: Matching 4 in a line makes a line-clearing rocket
An L or T shape makes a bomb (TNT)
A 2x2 square makes a propeller that flies to a target tile
Matching 5 in a line makes a colour-clearing light ball
Swapping two power-ups together creates a stronger combined effect
dynamics: Players set up combos instead of taking the first available match
The propeller rewards squares and helps reach awkward goal tiles
failure_modes: Too many power-ups per level devalues them; too few makes hard levels feel like luck

mechanics.name: Rescue-the-king special levels
mechanics.player_fantasy: Saving the hapless king from a comic disaster that worsens with every move.
rules: A special level type shows the king in peril; the player must reach the goal before the threat completes
dynamics: Urgency and humour in one beat
Breaks the rhythm of standard levels

mobile_fit.notes: Very short and readable at thumbnail size, which also makes it strong ad footage.

currencies.note: earned slowly from play and events, mainly bought; spent on extra moves, boosters and lives
one per win; spent on renovation tasks
lost on failure, regenerate over time, can be gifted by teammates

progression.structure: linear level map; one star per win drives the castle renovation track
progression.difficulty: regular hard and very hard levels flagged in the UI before starting, between easier levels
progression.boosters: unlock gradually in the early levels as the player meets new obstacles

top_offers: bundles of coins plus boosters and timed unlimited lives
monetization.ads: No interstitial or banner ads observed; verify on the current build.

liveops.pass: season pass with free and premium tracks
liveops.events: rotating time-limited events (competitions, streak and collection events); the roster changes often, so check the live build
liveops.cadence: overlapping events so there is always an active goal

retention_hooks: Unfinished renovation area with visible progress
Lives regenerate over time, so there is a reason to return later
Win-streak rewards that grant starting power-ups and reset on a loss
Team life requests create small obligations to return
Always-on event goals layered over the level map
social: teams with life requests and gifting
ux_notable: Very fast flow from map to level: few taps and short transitions
Hard levels are labelled before the attempt, which sets expectations and frames boosters
Goal panel stays compact and always visible; remaining moves are large and central
The extra-moves offer shows exactly which goals remain
art_audio_notable: High-contrast, saturated tiles with strong silhouettes that read at small sizes
Juicy, short power-up animations that do not slow the pace
Comedic king character carries tone in the meta and the special levels
psychology: Goal-gradient effect: renovation and event progress bars speed up play near completion
Loss aversion: the extra-moves offer arrives when only a few goals remain; streak rewards are lost on failure
Variable reward: cascades and combo outcomes
Zeigarnik effect: an unfinished renovation task stays visible on the home screen
innovations: A propeller power-up that flies to a target, which rewards a new match shape (the square)
Rescue-the-king levels used both as content and as ad creative
Pace: notably fast animations and level entry for the genre
weaknesses: Hard-level spikes push coin spending and frustrate non-payers (common review theme; verify against current reviews)
Renovation offers little player choice compared with decoration-choice metas
Lives gate long sessions for non-payers
lessons: Speed is a feature: cut every transition that does not deliver feedback
Label difficulty spikes up front; surprise difficulty feels unfair
A meta that shows visible progress for every win makes losses easier to accept
Special level formats can double as the ad creative, so design them for a 3-second read
borrow_for_us: One star per win spent on visible keep restoration, but restoration also unlocks golem families so the meta feeds the core
Hard-level labels on every 10th level of the sawtooth curve, shown before the attempt
Bonus Rune Sort levels as our special format: a calm breather (not a threat) that also gives a clean ad hook
Fast map-to-battle flow: at most 2 taps and under 1.5 s from the home keep to the first spawn
No lives system in the prototype: we test retention without energy gating first
